assumptions_made: Used the German Credit dataset from AiresPucrs/german-credit-data as it matches the required structure
Generated synthetic temporal data by repeating the base dataset and simulating drift every 3 months
Used logistic regression as baseline model for comparison
Implemented early stopping to prevent overfitting during training
Assumed that the dataset has enough samples to support 24 months of training
Since the dataset is small, we repeated it to simulate 24 months of data
Used a simple approach to simulate feature drift by slightly modifying numerical features
Trained models with early stopping based on validation loss to ensure convergence
Used standard evaluation metrics (Brier score and AUC-ROC) as specified in the plan

results.hypothesis: To determine whether adaptive ensemble methods maintain superior calibration performance (as measured by Brier score) compared to ranking discrimination (as measured by AUC-ROC) over a 24-month deployment period in consumer lending datasets subject to feature drift.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Performance of static models trained once on initial data without drift adaptation
results.success_criteria: If ensemble methods show consistently lower Brier scores and higher AUC-ROC values over time compared to baseline static models, the hypothesis is supported. If there is no significant difference or if ranking performance degrades faster than calibration, the hypothesis is refuted.
results.notes: Ensemble methods did not improve calibration (higher Brier score) compared to baseline.
